"Brand Signs In" --> "Connect Amazon / Flipkart via OAuth".
Rules loaded --> "Brand Voice Context Retrieved via pgvector".
Image Agent performs Vision Compliance Checks.
Content Agent --> "Outputs Merged into Canonical Listing JSON".
Keyword Agent --> Outputs Merged into Canonical Listing JSON.

The Correction Agent performs a field-level fix.
When a job is blocked, the reason is surfaced.
Connect: OAuth to Flipkart Seller API.
Tokens are encrypted at rest with AES-256.
Tokens are stored in the `MarketplaceAccount` table.
Token refresh is handled automatically by the adapters.
CSV upload enters the async queue.
Validated CSV rows are fanned out into parallel Agent Runs.
Agent Run fan-out uses bounded concurrency per marketplace to respect rate limits.
Brand voice is retrieved from pgvector embeddings.
Agents run in parallel where no dependencies exist.
Content, Keyword, Attribute, Image agents can execute concurrently.
Deterministic rules engine returns structured pass/fail via the unified ErrorReport.
Vision model returns structured pass/fail via the unified ErrorReport.
Human reviews the generated output alongside validation results.
Rejection feedback can be used as future context.
On partial success, only failed fields are retried.
Partial-success retries of only failed fields rely on idempotency keys on the marketplace side.
On partial success, the whole listing is never retried.
Performance metric conversion feeds the optimization loop.
Performance metric CTR feeds the optimization loop.
Performance metric returns feeds the optimization loop.
Performance metric ranking feeds the optimization loop.
The Optimization Agent proposes changes to existing listings based on performance data.
Table header: Failure Type | Response | Retry?
Rules engine failure: up to 3 agent correction attempts (bounded).
Rules engine failure retry: Yes — agent corrects specific field.
Rate limit handling has no agent involvement.
Auth failure response: auto-refresh token once.
Auth failure: escalate to user if still failing after refresh.
Auth failure retry: Once — then user action.
Partial API success response: retry only failed fields.
Partial API success response: never re-push the whole listing.
Partial API success retry: Yes — field-level.
JSON schema failure response: structured output repair.
JSON schema failure: escalate model if needed.
JSON schema failure retry: Yes — model escalation.
The brand uploads its product catalog once instead of writing separate listings per platform (example: clothing brand on Amazon and Flipkart).
The AI writes optimized listings for each marketplace using the brand's voice.
Non-technical explanation: the AI checks that images meet platform requirements.
Non-technical explanation: the AI validates everything against marketplace rules.
Non-technical explanation: the AI shows the brand owner the result for approval.
After the owner clicks "Approve", the listing goes live on both platforms.
Over time, the system learns which listings perform best and suggests improvements.
Page [8] Product Import Flow scope: MVP.
Products enter the system via CSV bulk upload (page description).
Products enter the system via manual entry (page description).
Products enter the system via catalog sync (page description).
Keywords: import, CSV, bulk, upload, product, catalog, manual entry
Table header: Mode | Use Case | Processing
CSV Bulk Upload use case: Large catalogs (100+ products).
CSV Bulk Upload processing: Async via Redis/ARQ queue.
CSV Bulk Upload processing: row-level validation.
CSV Bulk Upload processing: fan-out to parallel Agent Runs.
Manual Entry use case: Single product or quick addition.
Catalog Sync use case: Existing catalog integration.
Catalog Sync processing: Future: API-based sync with external catalog systems.
Mermaid fence and graph direction (graph TD).
Queue: Fan-out per Row --> "Product 1 Agent Run".
Product N Agent Run --> Aggregate Results.
Partial failures isolate to the row.
The batch completes with a summary report despite partial failures.
Bounded concurrency per marketplace respects rate limits.
Each product row is validated for required field: SKU.
Each product row is validated for required field: title.
Each product row is validated for required field: at least one image.
Each product row is validated for data types.
Each product row is validated for category existence.
Each product row is validated for marketplace compatibility.
Invalid rows are surfaced immediately with exact error details.
Valid rows proceed to agent generation.
Page [9] Marketplace Connection Flow scope: MVP.
Marketplace connection flow is OAuth-based for Amazon SP-API.
Marketplace connection flow is OAuth-based for Flipkart Seller API.
Keywords: marketplace, connection, OAuth, Amazon, Flipkart, SP-API, credentials
OAuth sequence participant FE: Next.js Frontend.
OAuth sequence participant BE: FastAPI Backend.
User clicks "Connect Amazon" in the frontend.
BE -> Marketplace: redirect to OAuth consent.
Marketplace displays consent screen to user.
Marketplace -> BE: callback with auth code.
BE -> Marketplace: exchange code for tokens.
BE stores encrypted tokens in MarketplaceAccount.
OAuth tokens encrypted at rest with AES-256.
Encryption keys stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
Encryption keys are never in application code.
Token refresh handled automatically by adapters.
Persistent token refresh failure escalates to user.
Each marketplace account is scoped to a tenant.
No cross-tenant access to marketplace accounts.

AI generates a complete listing from product data.
Listing generation stage: parallel agent execution.

Before any agent runs, the system assembles a rich context object.
Context object contains: brand voice chunks.
Brand voice chunks are retrieved via pgvector cosine similarity.
Context object contains: category template with required/optional attributes.
Context object contains: previous listing versions (if any).
Content Agent, Keyword Agent, Attribute Agent, and Image Agent can execute in parallel.
Content, Keyword, Attribute and Image Agents have no inter-dependencies (reason they can run in parallel).
Each agent reads from the shared context.
The Agent Orchestrator (LangGraph) manages this parallelism.
The Agent Orchestrator merges outputs into the canonical listing JSON.
LangGraph supports parallel node execution via branching edges.
Each agent node reads from the shared AgentState.
Each agent node writes to its own output field.
The merge node combines all outputs into the final canonical listing.

Stage 1: Schema Validation — correct data types.

The ErrorReport Contract is labelled "Unified ErrorReport".
JSON code fence and opening brace of the ErrorReport example.
ErrorReport field "errors": array of per-field error objects.
errors[] item field "message", example "Title is 221 chars; Amazon limit is 200".
Amazon title limit is 200 chars (per ErrorReport example).
errors[] item field "value_submitted", example "Organic Cotton Kurta Set... (221 chars)".
errors[] item field "suggestion", example "Shorten to <= 200 chars; move detail to bullets".
errors[] item "field" uses indexed path, example "bullets[2]".
errors[] item message example "Contains 'best' which is restricted on Flipkart".
The term 'best' is restricted on Flipkart (per ErrorReport example).
errors[] item value_submitted example "Best quality fabric...".
errors[] item suggestion example "Replace with factual claim, e.g. 'Premium quality fabric'".
errors[] item "retryable": true (repeated in second example).
Closing braces, array bracket and code fence of the ErrorReport example.
